citations.note: KTMP is ECOCROP's 'Killing Temperature' field. KTMP is ECOCROP's 'Killing Temperature' field (named as such in the Notes section of the official tutorial, .research-sources/2026-11-06/ecocrop-tutorial.pdf, p.4: 'Killing Temperature' is one of the described Notes headings). It is the single value closest in meaning to a damage limit (the crop is reported killed, not merely sub-optimal), but the tutorial does not state whether it is a daily-minimum air-temperature reading, an instantaneous low, or a multi-day exposure, nor the growth stage it applies to. KTMPR gives ECOCROP's stated reliability/tolerance range around KTMP, not a second stage. The builder could not re-find the quote in the saved text, so it is not reproduced.

citations.locator: EcoCrop_DB.csv row for ScientificName="Beta vulgaris"; field TMAX
citations.note: TMAX is ECOCROP's stated absolute upper bound of 'the full range of temperatures under which the plant will grow' (full adaptability range), not a stated daily-maximum air-temperature damage onset. The ECOCROP tutorial (.research-sources/2026-11-06/ecocrop-tutorial.pdf, p.2) defines TOPMN/TOPMX as 'the optimal growing temperature adaptability range (the range of temperatures under which the plant will grow optimally)' and TMIN/TMAX as part of 'the full growing temperature adaptability range (the full range of temperatures under which the plant will grow)... All entries are absolute values.' Neither definition states a daily-maximum or daily-minimum air-temperature basis, a duration, or a growth stage; ECOCROP's underlying climate matching (Hijmans et al.) compares these to long-run mean monthly temperatures, not single-day extremes. TMIN/TMAX are therefore NOT used here as whole-cycle damage limits outright; they are recorded as the closest FAO-tier evidence with this basis gap explicit in missingFields. The builder could not re-find the quote in the saved text, so it is not reproduced.

references.summary: Vegetable root crop selected for table use. Cool-season adaptation does not supply an exact daily-minimum injury boundary; cold can affect bolting. High heat and water stress can impair root quality and growth. It can share some Beta-associated problems with sugar beet; a sugar-beet rotation rule needs product and pathogen context. Harvest size and cultivar affect the cycle; fresh-root yield differs from sugar-beet root or sugar yield.
